_meta.indication: Indicated to help the prevention of sunburn and to help provide protection from UVA and UVB rays, for OTC daily use by adults and children at least 6 months of age

pivotal_trials.design: Controlled, randomized, evaluator blind, intra-individual study design in healthy volunteers at a single center, using an 8% Homosalate standard sunscreen as reference
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy volunteers between the ages of 18 and 65 years old with fair skin types (I, II, or III) and intact skin in the treatment area
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sun protection factor (SPF), defined as MED of protected skin / MED of unprotected skin
pivotal_trials.result: Mean SPF ± SD of test formulation 539-009 was 16.65 ± 3.57 (95% CI 15.3 to 17.9), resulting in a labeled SPF of 15

pivotal_trials.design: Controlled, randomized, evaluator blind, intra-individual study design in healthy volunteers at a single center, using an 8% Homosalate standard sunscreen as reference
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy volunteers between the ages of 18 and 65 years old with fair skin types (I, II, or III) and intact skin in the treatment area
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Sun protection factor (SPF), defined as MED of protected skin / MED of unprotected skin
pivotal_trials.result: Mean SPF ± SD of test formulation 539-009 was 17.45 ± 2.78 (95% CI 16.15 to 18.75), resulting in a labeled SPF of 16

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 910.01 (UVA protection factor / PFA determination study)
pivotal_trials.design: Controlled, randomized, evaluator blind, intra-individual study design in healthy volunteers at a single center; PFA determined by the minimal persistent pigment darkening (PPD) method
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy volunteers between 18 and 65 years old with skin phototypes II, III, or IV and intact skin in the treatment area
pivotal_trials.endpoint: UVA protection factor (PFA), defined as PPD of protected skin / PPD of unprotected skin
pivotal_trials.n: 30 evaluable subjects completed (only ten subjects evaluable per test formulation due to a protocol deviation)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean PFA ± SD of formulation 539-009 was 19.53 ± 3.39, versus standard sunscreen 4.05 ± 0.59; demonstrated effective UVA protection

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 920.01 (UVA protection factor / PFA determination study using the 8-MOP method)
pivotal_trials.design: Phototoxic erythema was measured using the 8-methoxypsoralen (8-MOP) method; no standard sunscreen was used and effectiveness was measured against untreated (control) sites
pivotal_trials.population: Healthy volunteers between 18 and 65 years old with skin phototypes I, II, or III and intact skin in the treatment area
pivotal_trials.endpoint: UVA protection factor (PFA), defined as MPD of protected skin / MPD of unprotected skin
pivotal_trials.result: Mean PFA ± SD of formulation 539-009 was 27.65 ± 10.91 by the 8-MOP method; results could not be validated in the absence of a concomitant standard but were comparable to the PPD-method results

key_safety: Acceptable OTC safety profile; most frequently reported adverse events were local application skin reactions (erythema, dermatitis, pruritus, edema, dry skin, skin irritation) or signs of eye irritation, with incidences not significantly different in children versus adults. In supportive studies there were 7 (2.1%) events of erythema/edema and 4 (1.2%) of papules considered treatment-related.
target_moa: Topical combination sunscreen (ecamsule 2%, avobenzone 2%, octocrylene 10%) that protects against UV radiation by absorption, scattering and reflection of incident UVR; ecamsule and avobenzone act as UVA filters and octocrylene acts mainly as a UVB filter, providing protection across the UVA and UVB spectrum
modality: small molecule (topical combination sunscreen of three small-molecule UV filters; ecamsule is a new molecular entity)

priority_review.basis: Priority Designation listed as 'S' (Standard) on the clinical review cover page, confirming the application was not granted priority review

summary.text: NDA 21-502 was submitted May 12, 2005 as a 505(b)(2) application for Anthelios SX, a topical OTC combination sunscreen containing the new molecular entity ecamsule plus avobenzone and octocrylene. The FDA issued an approvable letter on March 10, 2006 for labeling deficiencies and trade-name concerns; the sponsor's May 18, 2006 complete response resolved these and the NDA was approved on July 21, 2006, with a deferred PREA pediatric study required for patients under 6 months of age.
